'Didn’t you hear the cannon last night?'

Mrs. Joe re-entering the kitchen empty-handed, to stop short and stare, in her wondering lament of 'Gracious goodness gracious me, what’s gone—with the—pie!'
The sergeant and I were in the kitchen when Mrs. Joe stood staring.
The sergeant who had spoken to me, and he was now looking round at the company, with his handcuffs invitingly extended towards them in his right hand, and his left on my shoulder.
The sergeant said, 'Excuse me, ladies and gentleman, but as I have mentioned at the door to this smart young shaver, I am on a chase in the name of the king, and I want the blacksmith.'
Joe threw his eye over them, and pronounced that the job would necessitate the lighting of his forge fire, and would take nearer two hours than one.

The sergeant called to his men, who came trooping into the kitchen one after another, and piled their arms in a corner.

The soldiers stood about, as soldiers do; now, with their hands loosely clasped before them; now, resting a knee or a shoulder; now, easing a belt or a pouch; now, opening the door to spit stiffly over their high stocks, out into the yard.
I was in an agony of apprehension.

Mr. Wopsle, Joe, and I, received strict charge to keep in the rear, and to speak no word after we reached the marshes.
When we were all out in the raw air and were steadily moving towards our business, I treasonably whispered to Joe, 'I hope, Joe, we shan’t find them.'

We passed the finger-post, and held straight on to the churchyard.

They came in again without finding anything, and then we struck out on the open marshes, through the gate at the side of the churchyard.
A bitter sleet came rattling against us here on the east wind, and Joe took me on his back.

The soldiers made for the shouting at a greater rate than ever, and we after them.

The sergeant struggled at the bottom of a ditch.

My convict said, 'I took him! I give him up to you! Mind that!'

My convict said, 'I took him, and giv’ him up; that’s what I done.'

The sergeant made some kind of report, and some entry in a book.
